english.title: Bind over after complaint - breach of the peace caused
english.standardoffencewording:
On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..) behaved in a manner whereby a breach of the peace was occasioned.

The complaint is made by **(..SPECIFY NAME..) who applies for an order requiring that you enter into a recognisance with or without sureties to keep the peace
english.legislation: Pursuant to section 115 of the Magistrates' Courts Act 1980.
english.pointstoprove:
behaved in a manner
whereby a breach of the peace
was occasioned

investigatoraction.description: Confirm proposed charge is appropriately authorised (Police or CPS)
Ensure compliance with investigator's obligations re disclosure
Consider if case suitable for referral to Financial Investigation Unit and CPS for asset recovery eg confiscation order

english.notes:
(i) This complaint is for use in limited circumstances and must be laid against that person by the victim. The common law bind over can be used to stop any anti-social behaviour which amounts to a breach of the peace.
(ii) See H4636 - where a breach of the peace was likely to be occasioned.
(iii) This is NOT a fingerprintable or photographable offence.
(iv) See H4635 for bind overs following arrest (breach of the peace at common law).

welsh.welshoffencetitle: Rhwymo ar ôl cwyn - achosi torheddwch
welsh.welshstandardoffencewording:
Ar **(..SPECIFY DATE..) yn **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..) bu i chi ymddwyn mewn ffordd a achosodd dor-heddwch.

Gwneir y gwyn gan **(..SPECIFY NAME..) sy'n gwneud cais am orchymyn i'ch gorfodi i wneud ymrwymiad i gadw'r heddwch gyda meichiau neu hebddynt
welsh.welshlegislation: Yn unol ag adran 115 Deddf Llysoedd Ynadon 1980.

other.powersofarrest: power of arrest for breach of peace
other.penalty:
The party against whom the complaint was laid may be bound over to keep the peace.

Time limit for prosecutions:
6 months

libra.complexpenaltydetails: The party against whom the complaint was laid may be bound over to keep the peace.

ancillary.lastupdate: 031110 DVLA Code removed - this is NOT an offence as such it is a "complaint" made to the court and as such a DVLA Code does not apply.
